subject.title: fix(maint): refuse unsafe PR ancestry rewrites

question: Should rewritten PR histories fail closed and require the explicit ancestry-preserving git push override instead of continuing through GitHub’s verified GraphQL commit path?
rationale: The code can enforce only one of these operational properties: verified append-only GraphQL commits or preserved rewritten ancestry; accepting the new maintainer step is an intentional workflow tradeoff.

options.title: Accept fail-closed ancestry handling
options.body: Land the patch and require maintainers to review rewritten commits before using the explicit ancestry-preserving git push override.

options.title: Pause for another push mechanism
options.body: Hold the PR until a signed or otherwise verified ancestry-preserving push mechanism is available without the manual override.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed ancestry handling
recommendation.body: Land the patch and require maintainers to review rewritten commits before using the explicit ancestry-preserving git push override.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows direct ownership of the shared preparation and sync-evidence workflow, and this PR carries the intended operator policy.
